lines.speaker: Barnaby Velvet
lines.text: You're in the Lounge at the End of Time. Pull up a booth. There's no hurry. There's no anything.

lines.speaker: Barnaby Velvet
lines.text: The Lounge at the End of Time. Ninety-two point six. Last call has been going on for eleven billion years.

lines.speaker: Barnaby Velvet
lines.text: Good evening. This is the Lounge at the End of Time. It's always evening here. We arranged it.

lines.speaker: Barnaby Velvet
lines.text: The Lounge at the End of Time. Where everything ends... beautifully.

lines.speaker: Barnaby Velvet
lines.text: You're listening to the Lounge at the End of Time. Gilbert, another round for the listener.

lines.speaker: Gilbert (Bartender)
lines.text: On it.

lines.speaker: Barnaby Velvet
lines.text: Good morning, if you'll allow it. The Lounge at the End of Time is still open. We never really closed.

lines.speaker: Barnaby Velvet
lines.text: The Lounge at the End of Time. Heat Death Boulevard. Mind the step. It's the last one.

lines.speaker: Barnaby Velvet
lines.text: That was a real heartbreaker. I don't say that lightly. I've said it about every song I've ever played, and I have meant it, every single time. Here's another.

lines.speaker: Barnaby Velvet
lines.text: If you're seated by the big window, you'll have noticed another star went out just then, over to the left. Lovely little thing. Burned for nine billion years. Never once complained.

lines.speaker: Barnaby Velvet
lines.text: Let's raise a glass to her. And now, a real heartbreaker.

lines.speaker: Barnaby Velvet
lines.text: Gilbert tells me it's last call. Gilbert has been telling me it's last call for eleven billion years. I've never once taken him up on it, and I think, deep down, he's grateful.

lines.speaker: Gilbert (Bartender)
lines.text: I am not.

lines.speaker: Barnaby Velvet
lines.text: He is.

lines.speaker: Barnaby Velvet
lines.text: To the gentleman in booth four: your tab is still open. It has been open since the formation of the first galaxies. We don't mind in the least.

lines.speaker: Barnaby Velvet
lines.text: We simply think it's worth mentioning, as the galaxies are now leaving.

lines.speaker: Barnaby Velvet
lines.text: The microphone on our little stage is empty tonight, as it is every night. We keep the spotlight on, just in case. Someone might come. Someone always might come.

lines.speaker: Barnaby Velvet
lines.text: Until then, here's a real heartbreaker.

lines.speaker: Barnaby Velvet
lines.text: There's a shadow at the end of the bar. No one attached. Orders a dry ginger, tips well, says his name is Greg. Barely speaks.

lines.speaker: Barnaby Velvet
lines.text: I think he's waiting for somebody, or hiding from somebody, which at this hour is the same thing. Somebody called Hollis, I gather. Greg, darling. Call home.

lines.speaker: Barnaby Velvet
lines.text: This evening's music comes to you courtesy of Grumbel's Ladders. At the end of time, darling, everyone wants to see just a little bit further. Grumbel's. Up is a choice. While there's still an up.

lines.speaker: Barnaby Velvet
lines.text: It's late. Later than it's ever been, if we're honest, and getting later all the time. Let's not worry about that. Let's worry about whether you've got enough ice. Gilbert?

lines.speaker: Gilbert (Bartender)
lines.text: They've got enough ice.

lines.speaker: Barnaby Velvet
lines.text: There we are. Here's a song.

lines.speaker: Barnaby Velvet
lines.text: Good evening. The universe is cooling nicely tonight, a gentle three degrees above nothing at all. Perfect weather for a slow dance.

lines.speaker: Barnaby Velvet
lines.text: Find someone. If there's no one left, find a coat stand. Coat stands are wonderful listeners.

lines.speaker: Barnaby Velvet
lines.text: Somebody asked me once if I ever tire of calling a song a real heartbreaker. And I said, darling, the day I stop meaning it is the day I close the lid on the piano.

lines.speaker: Barnaby Velvet
lines.text: The lid is open. Here's a real heartbreaker.

lines.speaker: Barnaby Velvet
lines.text: A word of thanks to Gilbert, our bartender, who is polishing eight glasses at once again tonight. I asked him why. He said, Barnaby, because I can.

lines.speaker: Barnaby Velvet
lines.text: Which is the most beautiful answer I have ever heard to anything.

lines.speaker: Barnaby Velvet
lines.text: If you're joining us in the morning, wherever mornings still happen, welcome. We don't serve breakfast. We serve the last of the olives. Which is breakfast, eventually.

lines.speaker: Barnaby Velvet
lines.text: To everyone listening alone tonight. You're not. There's me. There's Gilbert. There's the shadow at the end of the bar.

lines.speaker: Barnaby Velvet
lines.text: And there's the whole slow, golden end of everything, just out the big window, putting on a show for you. Here's a real heartbreaker.

lines.speaker: Barnaby Velvet
lines.text: Afternoon, at the end of time. The light through the big window is the colour of a peach that's been thinking about things. Here's something to sip.

lines.speaker: Barnaby Velvet
lines.text: That last number was recorded in this very room, the night the final supernova went off. You can hear the whole audience gasp at the bridge.

lines.speaker: Barnaby Velvet
lines.text: That's the supernova. It was gorgeous. Here's another.

lines.speaker: Barnaby Velvet
lines.text: Gilbert, what's the most anyone's ever ordered at last call?

lines.speaker: Gilbert (Bartender)
lines.text: Eleven billion years of last calls. One at a time.

lines.speaker: Barnaby Velvet
lines.text: Pacing, darling. It's all about pacing. Here's a slow one.

lines.speaker: Barnaby Velvet
lines.text: We have a call in the last booth. Hello, you're at the Lounge.

lines.speaker: Bev
lines.text: Hello, love. It's Bev. I'm still looking for the request line.

lines.speaker: Barnaby Velvet
lines.text: Bev. We've been expecting you. You may request anything. Sing it for me.

lines.speaker: Bev
lines.text: Da da dum. Da da.

lines.speaker: Barnaby Velvet
lines.text: Gilbert. Did you hear that?

lines.speaker: Gilbert (Bartender)
lines.text: I did.

lines.speaker: Barnaby Velvet
lines.text: Bev, I don't know it. But I want you to know. It's a real heartbreaker.

lines.speaker: Bev
lines.text: That's what I keep saying, love!
